title: A w-contractible affine pro-etale object is weakly contractible
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be an object of this site. Suppose that every faithfully flat ring map $A\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] which is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] admits a ring retraction $B\to A$, whose composite with $A\to B$ is $\mathrm{id}_A$. Then for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the evaluation map $F(T)\to G(T)$ is surjective. Here a sheaf of sets is a contravariant set-valued functor on the site satisfying unique gluing of compatible sections on every covering; a morphism is a natural transformation, and an epimorphism is a morphism that is right-cancellable among such morphisms.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:F\to G$ be an epimorphism and $s\in G(T)$, where $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By the epimorphism/local-surjectivity equivalence the image sieve of $s$ is covering. A covering sieve contains a family in the pro-etale precoverage. Restrict this family to a small covering subfamily $\{g_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ and choose lifts $t_i\in F(T_i)$ with $\alpha(t_i)=G(g_i)(s)$. This restriction uses the existing Mathlib smallness instance for the quasi-compact weakly etale precoverage, its stability under comap, and ZeroHypercover.restrictIndexOfSmall; it changes only the indexing of a subfamily and preserves both covering and local lifts.

source.place: Tags 00WM and 00WN; small-cover indexing uses Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/QuasiCompact.lean and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Hypercover/Zero.lean

proof.text: Form $C=\coprod_iT_i$ and $p=\coprod_i g_i:C\to T$. Convert the ring-map splitting hypothesis to the equivalent algebra formulation, using RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff and RingHom.weaklyEtale_algebraMap_iff. The covering-section lemma gives $\sigma:T\to C$ with $\sigma\mathbin{\gg}p=\mathrm{id}_T$. Each $g_i$ is weakly etale because the underlying family belongs to the pro-etale precoverage. Source locality gives weak etaleness of $p$ (Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc), so the composite $C\to T\to X$ is weakly etale. Consequently $C$, $p$, and $\sigma$ belong to the same small site over $X$, with coprojections $\iota_i:T_i\to C$ satisfying $\iota_i\mathbin{\gg}p=g_i$.

source.place: Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, forward proof; glue before pulling back the coproduct components

proof.text: The coprojections form a disjoint open cover of $C$ and hence a pro-etale cover in the small site. In Lean this is the coproduct open cover together with Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage and the defining comap of the small precoverage. The family $t_i$ is compatible: for two maps from a test object into the same component whose composites into $C$ agree, monomorphy makes the maps equal. For maps into distinct components the test scheme is empty, by disjointness of their images. The empty covering gives a unique section of $F$ on that test object, so the two restrictions coincide. Apply the sheaf axiom to obtain $z\in F(C)$ restricting to every $t_i$. This works for the empty index type as well, without a nontriviality assumption on $A$.

source.place: Tag 098H, lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible, disjoint-cover product/gluing argument; applied to the covering coproduct itself

proof.text: Naturality gives $G(\iota_i)(\alpha(z))=\alpha(t_i)=G(g_i)(s)=G(\iota_i)(G(p)(s))$. Separatedness of $G$ for the coprojection cover gives $\alpha(z)=G(p)(s)$. Pull back $z$ along $\sigma$. Naturality and contravariant functoriality yield $\alpha(F(\sigma)(z))=G(\sigma)(G(p)(s))=G(\sigma\mathbin{\gg}p)(s)=s$. Thus the evaluation map is surjective. No finite clopen refinement of $T$ is needed: gluing on $C$ before pullback gives exactly the same preimage.
